name: Continuum
tagline: Small indie tool for keeping one continuous thread of your notes, work and AI conversation context.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Public detail on this one is thin, so treat the read as category-level rather than product-level. A single-user store of notes and context, searchable and exportable into whatever model you are talking to today, is squarely inside what a coding agent can produce in a sitting: SQLite, full text search, a timeline, a copy-context button. The parts that take real time are the ones nobody enjoys building, namely sync across devices, a mobile client, and the small interaction touches that make a capture tool something you actually reach for. Expect a working local version fast and a version you trust with your whole life much later. If the product turns out to lean on proprietary retrieval or model behavior rather than storage plus search, the gap widens.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app that captures dated notes and snippets, indexes them for search, and assembles a copy-paste context bundle for any AI chat.
requirements: Local disk for the SQLite file
Optional API key in .env if you want model-side summarizing
whatYouLose: Device sync and any mobile capture surface
Whatever polish makes capture friction-free instead of a chore
Browser or OS integrations that pull context in automatically
Someone else maintaining backups, migrations and the search index
Any smart retrieval work the product may have tuned that a plain FTS5 query will not match
moatNotes: Personal context tools win on daily friction, not architecture. Once a year of your notes lives inside one, leaving is annoying by design.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the bottleneck is never the database, it is whether you open the thing at 11pm with a half-formed thought. A paid tool that syncs to your phone, launches in a keystroke and never loses an entry earns its money against a local build you stop touching in three weeks. Add the fact that the value compounds with accumulated entries, and the switching cost is real even if the code is not hard.
notes: Storage plus search is a weekend, the habit is not.
prompt:
Build a local-first personal context tool called Continuum. Single user, runs on my machine, no accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, no substitutions:
- TypeScript everywhere
- Hono server on Node 20, serving both the API and the built frontend on port 4321
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, single file at ./data/continuum.db, WAL mode
- FTS5 virtual table for search
- React with Vite for the UI, plain CSS, no component library

Data model:
- entries: id, created_at, updated_at, body (markdown), source (manual | clipboard | file), pinned (bool)
- tags and entry_tags, tags parsed from #hashtags in the body on save
- entries_fts kept in sync with triggers on insert, update, delete

Features in scope:
- Capture box always focused on load, cmd+enter saves, stays open for the next thought
- Reverse chronological timeline, infinite scroll, grouped by day
- Search bar hitting FTS5 with snippet highlighting, filter by tag, filter by date range
- Edit and soft delete an entry (deleted_at column, no hard deletes)
- Context bundle: select entries by search or tag, click Copy Context, get one markdown block with dates and bodies, token estimate shown next to the button
- Export everything to a folder of dated markdown files, and import that folder back
- npm run backup copies the db file with a timestamp

Explicitly out of scope: auth, multi-user, sync, mobile app, embeddings, model calls, background jobs, Docker.

Secrets, if any are ever added, go in .env read via process.env, and .env is gitignored.

Deliver: npm install, npm run dev for hot reload, npm run build then npm start for the real thing. Seed script that inserts 30 fake entries across 60 days so search and grouping are visible. A README with the schema and the keyboard shortcuts. Vitest tests for the FTS triggers and the context bundle assembly.
